2026-11-06, lane C of the automata program (`SUBSTRATE-DECISION.md` §4). Tags: [MEASURED] a pinned
`#guard` at the cited `file:line` (the generator re-reads every cited line and refuses to print if
one moved); [READ] read off an emitted golden or a note; [INFERRED] a model number. Counts, not clocks.

Two blocks per family, kept apart on purpose (codex round 3, finding 16): the **semantic** operation
counts (what the checker does per symbol) and the **BabyBear realization** (what the served
descriptor spends). A "lookup" is an abstract operation; its realization cost (LogUp auxiliary
columns, table authentication) belongs to the target and is not pinned in Lean today. Tower256 has
no AIR layer yet (LEAF-PROVER-DECISION §6 "not yet available"), so it has a commitment column and
no realization column.

Notes on the rows [READ unless tagged]:
- table routing's exact-public table IS the run: unit-capacity exact-public receives pin the trace
  length to the declared rows (`metatheory/Dregg2/Circuit/Emit/TinyAutomataLanesK.lean:784`, `forcedTraceRows := .pinned 8` at word length 8), so the
  descriptor grows with the word and the word is public. That is the served shape today; a private-word
  table routing needs a committed transition table (the weld's shape) or a LogUp table of `|Q|·|Σ|` rows.
- the weld is over binary symbols (`metatheory/Dregg2/Circuit/Emit/AttestedAutomatonEmit.lean:164`); a byte costs 8 rows, each with
  `MAP_TREE_DEPTH` = 16 chip permutations of map authentication (`metatheory/Dregg2/Circuit/Emit/AttestedAutomatonWeld8.lean:980`).
- Dyck: the deployed grammar caps nesting at k ≤ 3, so its language is `[ᵏ]ᵏ` for k ≤ 3, at most
  6 tokens; record-size rows below are n/a, not a cost.
- degree: no emitter pins a maximum constraint degree; the column says where each number was read.
- names are the descriptors' own `name` fields. The served toggle `dfa-routing-toggle-2state::poseidon2-v1`
  comes from `metatheory/Dregg2/Circuit/Emit/DfaRoutingEmit.lean` [READ `circuit/src/descriptor_by_name.rs:83`];
  the 3-state injection object `DfaRoutingGeneralEmit` emits is not routed by name.

## 3. Commitment term (once per record, shared by every statement over the same `c`)

BabyBear: `hash_bytes_8`, `⌈n/8⌉+2` Poseidon2 permutations × 352 cells [READ `circuit/src/poseidon2.rs:704`;
the +2 is the length lanes' absorb and the squeeze]. Tower256 [INFERRED, all of it]: cSHAKE256 over
byte-aligned input with a 32-byte output costs `⌊n/136⌋ + 1` Keccak-f including padding (FIPS 202
Algorithm 8; the first output block needs no extra squeeze), plus one block for the cSHAKE `bytepad(N, S)`
prefix (SP 800-185 §3.3) unless that state is precomputed ("cold" below counts it). The "31 per 4 KiB" of
LEAF-PROVER-DECISION §1 is the **payload sponge only**, not the commitment price: the leaf commits by a
Merkle root, modelled here over 32-byte leaves (§7's 66-byte unary / 37-byte u32 leaf inputs), one Keccak-f
per leaf and per node.

| n bytes | BabyBear perms | BabyBear cells | Keccak-f payload sponge (warm / cold prefix) | Keccak-f Merkle, 32-B leaves (warm / cold) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 34 | 11,968 | 2 / 3 | 15 / 30 |
| 4,096 | 514 | 180,928 | 31 / 32 | 255 / 510 |
| 65,536 | 8,194 | 2,884,288 | 482 / 483 | 4,095 / 8,190 |

Commitment sharing: one `c` serves every statement over the same record bytes under the same scheme
(the DFA, product, and padded-complement runs over one record share it). A BabyBear `c` and a Tower256
`c` are different objects; the weld's 8-felt root commits the automaton, not the record, and is a
second commitment.

## 4. The two hot spots, with the binary length lane

**Unary length framing** (`Tower256CshakeMerkleController.encodeLength n` = n zero bytes then 1;
`hashLeaf` absorbs `0 :: envelope b`, i.e. 2n+2 bytes for an n-byte payload) [READ minidregg
Compiler/Tower256CshakeMerkleController.lean, quoted in zkml-research LEAF-PROVER-DECISION §7].
In the run term it is one padding row per symbol wherever the byte column absorbs the framed payload;
a u32 length lane (LEAF-PROVER-DECISION §7) makes it 4 rows. In the sponge it doubles the absorbed bytes.
Inside 32-byte Merkle leaves it costs nothing (66 and 37 bytes are both one block).

[INFERRED: the saving applies where a family's byte column absorbs the framed payload; no served descriptor does today.]

| n bytes | framing rows unary → u32 | rows saved | table-routing main cells saved (×3) | weld8 main cells saved (×8 rows × 11) | flat-sponge Keccak-f unary → u32 | Merkle Keccak-f unary → u32 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 257 → 4 | 253 | 759 | 22,264 | 4 → 2 | 15 → 15 |
| 4,096 | 4,097 → 4 | 4,093 | 12,279 | 360,184 | 61 → 31 | 255 → 255 |
| 65,536 | 65,537 → 4 | 65,533 | 196,599 | 5,766,904 | 964 → 482 | 4,095 → 4,095 |

**`⌈n/8⌉+2` Poseidon2 permutations** are the BabyBear commitment; they do not transfer. The same record on

## 5. Datalog: per firing, and the universal leg

- One rule firing (`DerivationEmit`): 386 columns (`metatheory/Dregg2/Circuit/Emit/DerivationEmit.lean:393`), 393 constraints
  (`metatheory/Dregg2/Circuit/Emit/DerivationEmit.lean:397`), 13 PIs (`metatheory/Dregg2/Circuit/Emit/DerivationEmit.lean:398`); degree 8 [READ hub §2; unpinned]. Per
  firing, not per symbol.
- The closure (universal) leg of `FixpointCert.verify` enumerates, per rule r, every substitution over the
  active domain: Σ_r |dom|^varBound(r) candidates, each a body check. `activeDomain` is
  `edb.flatMap (·.2) ++ P.flatMap ruleConsts` (`metatheory/Dregg2/Datalog/FixpointCert.lean:139`), a LIST with duplicates, so the
  executable count is larger than the set count. Pinned on the transitive-closure example: |dom| = 6
  (`metatheory/Dregg2/Datalog/FixpointCert.lean:642`), 6³ = 216 candidates for the 3-variable step rule (`metatheory/Dregg2/Datalog/FixpointCert.lean:643`).
- Not arithmetized: the fixpoint and the closure leg have no descriptor; their cost is checker steps.
